findings: J101.5 now joins R1021.2 and R1031.1 in one BAT_ADC group; R1021.1 to U1001.3 is still open.
No parts move. Twenty-five new segments replace twelve old ones; one new GND via and one 0.08 mm move of an existing HEAD_BUCK_IN via.
The new front ADC route clears the right-side connector guards and its thermal spokes. The bottom run turns outside the nominal housing; one necessary pin-5 outward escape is explicitly recorded.
The upper existing FAULT branch moves to its already-allowed In2 corridor; the lower front detour preserves the original connected FAULT group. Three other FAULT gaps remain.
The HEAD_BUCK_IN In2 allocation grows by exactly 1.65 mm2. Source priority 20, clearance 0.4 mm, fill minimum 0.25 mm, thermal settings and all native rules remain unchanged.
Before/after In2 plots show the north-side power neck restored. The old 0.80/0.40 mm power via moves from (45.4,29.1) to (45.48,29.1), with a rebuilt 0.80 mm back trace to unchanged D901.1.
All 50 supply-width, 155 ground-pad, 63 adjacency and old/new reference checks pass. Ground via (45.65,30) actually contacts F, In1, In4 and B ground. Six historical transition flags remain.
same_face_exception: J101.5 straight outward connector escape through the nominal housing lip only; all native keepouts preserved. Not zero body overlap or measured fit.

projection_review.review: The F.Cu BAT_ADC escape goes straight outward from pin 5 through only its nominal housing lip, then turns below the body. Its 0.0762582306 mm2 outside-pad nominal projection is a documented connector escape exception, not zero overlap. Native keepouts are intact. The inner FAULT route passes under the other end of this fixed header with intervening In1 ground. Mating, actual envelope and thermal/EMC qualification remain open.

The F.Cu BAT_ADC escape goes straight outward from pin 5 through only its nominal housing lip, then turns below the body. Its 0.0762582306 mm2 outside-pad nominal projection is a documented connector escape exception, not zero overlap. Native keepouts are intact. The inner FAULT route passes under the other end of this fixed header with intervening In1 ground. Mating, actual envelope and thermal/EMC qualification remain open.

The front FAULT branch projects opposite the fixed back AO3400A fault transistor. Intervening In1/In4 reference ground and native clearances were inspected; existing transistor connections are unchanged. Local reference continuity is not switching-coupling or temperature qualification.

The In2 FAULT branch projects below the front 100k battery-divider resistor with intervening In1 ground. The front ADC exits its actual pad outward and no longer grazes the nominal body outside that pad. The replacement ground path reaches an actual stitch contacting both reference planes. Divider settling, injected error and temperature effects remain unqualified.

The bottom-edge front ADC trace projects opposite the fixed back 100k HEAD_UV_N pull-up. In1/In4 ground remains between the faces and all existing pull-up power/ground connectivity is preserved. Reference screening does not establish ADC accuracy or cross-coupling performance.

The front resistor-to-resistor ADC segment projects opposite the fixed back TPS3700DDCR monitor, separated by the reference planes. The monitor connections and neighboring supply widths are unchanged. Transient coupling, sensing accuracy and heat remain unqualified.

limits: Nominal Fab/fallback envelopes are not manufacturer maximum or measured body dimensions.
Native plots do not depict every through-hole drill cut distinctly; actual native pad/drill geometry governs.
Local supply width is a geometry screen, not ampacity or thermal qualification.
Whole-board routing style, six historical transitions, parasitics, mechanical fit and physical tests remain open.
